quarterly_data.quarter: Resonac (Showa Denko) annual securities report: FY2025 (03-25-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: FY2025 (January-December 2025): revenue fell as only the Semiconductor & Electronic Materials segment grew (on higher sales volume) while the other four segments declined; core operating profit rose on the Semiconductor & Electronic Materials gain. Operating profit fell on impairment losses tied to decisions to transfer several businesses, including Fiamm Energy Technology S.p.A. (the prior year had a gain on the sale of the former head-office land and building). Semiconductor & Electronic Materials: front-end materials slightly lower on the slow pace of NAND demand recovery and the transfer of the exhaust-gas treatment equipment business; back-end materials higher mainly on higher sales volume for advanced semiconductors such as AI; HD media higher on solid data-center demand; SiC epitaxial wafers flat as EV market growth slowed. No single customer accounted for 10% or more of revenue from external customers.
quarterly_data.figure: Revenue JPY 1,347,125 million (-3.2%); core operating profit JPY 109,145 million (+18.4%); operating profit JPY 46,676 million (-47.6%); profit attributable to owners of parent JPY 29,031 million; Semiconductor & Electronic Materials revenue JPY 506,336 million (+13.7%), core operating profit JPY 108,365 million (+47.0%)

quarterly_data.quarter: Resonac (Showa Denko) annual securities report: FY2025 (03-25-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: FY2025 results of the other segments: Mobility lower on the January-March transfer of the battery packaging and food packaging businesses and weaker demand from some domestic customers; Innovation Materials lower as demand for some products fell with the weak auto market; Chemical lower as graphite electrode volumes and prices both fell (graphite loss widened) while chemicals rose on higher carbon dioxide gas volume and price increases for some products; Crasus Chemical lower on naphtha-linked selling price declines and weaker product markets.
quarterly_data.figure: Mobility revenue JPY 178,430 million (-10.9%), core operating profit JPY 4,396 million; Innovation Materials revenue JPY 92,202 million (-4.9%), core operating profit JPY 10,352 million; Chemical revenue JPY 174,358 million (-14.0%), core operating profit JPY -5,484 million; Crasus Chemical revenue JPY 300,302 million (-8.9%), core operating profit JPY 4,698 million

quarterly_data.quarter: Resonac (Showa Denko) annual securities report: FY2025 (03-25-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Long-term numerical targets (company): revenue above JPY 1 trillion, EBITDA margin 20%, ROIC 10%, net D/E ratio 1.0x or below; the company states that against the backdrop of growing semiconductor demand it will keep investing aggressively in its core growth business, semiconductor and electronic materials, while continuing business portfolio reform.
quarterly_data.figure: Targets: EBITDA margin 20% (2025 actual 15.1%), ROIC 10% (2025 actual 6.2%), revenue above JPY 1 trillion (2025 actual JPY 1.35 trillion)

quarterly_data.quarter: Resonac (Showa Denko) annual securities report: FY2025 (03-25-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: FY2025 capital expenditure (including right-of-use assets); in Semiconductor & Electronic Materials, Resonac expanded production capacity for CMP slurry (front-end), dicing die-bonding integrated film (die-bonding material) and copper-clad laminates for semiconductor package substrates. In the capex plan for the year after FY2025, Semiconductor & Electronic Materials covers capacity expansion of copper-clad laminates for semiconductor package substrates plus expansion, rationalisation and maintenance.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2025 capex JPY 112,853 million (Semiconductor & Electronic Materials JPY 64,064 million); next-year capex plan JPY 146,234 million (Semiconductor & Electronic Materials JPY 83,696 million, Mobility JPY 13,243 million, Innovation Materials JPY 8,737 million, Chemical JPY 13,277 million, Crasus Chemical JPY 15,296 million)

quarterly_data.quarter: Resonac (Showa Denko) annual securities report: FY2025 (03-25-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Back-end semiconductor materials R&D: for high-performance devices such as AI semiconductors the company is securing supply of laminate materials for package substrates (MCL) and increasing production capacity of non-conductive film (NCF) and thermal interface sheets (TIM). It developed a new high-resolution photosensitive film for advanced packaging that forms fine copper wiring with 1.5 micrometre line/space on organic interposers. Building on the JOINT2 and US-JOINT consortia, it founded JOINT3, a co-creation evaluation platform of 27 materials, equipment and design companies from Japan, the US, Singapore and elsewhere, with a base inside the Shimodate plant (Minami-Yuki) preparing to start operation during 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: 1.5 micrometre line/space on organic interposer; JOINT3: 27 companies, operation start targeted during 2026; Semiconductor & Electronic Materials R&D expense JPY 22,747 million (group R&D JPY 46,458 million)

quarterly_data.quarter: Resonac (Showa Denko) annual securities report: FY2025 (03-25-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Device solutions R&D: Resonac, which describes itself as the only merchant hard-disk media maker, is jointly developing next-generation hard disks for heat-assisted magnetic recording with Seagate Technology, and ships a shingled-recording product with what it calls the industry's highest capacity of 3.1 terabytes per platter on an aluminium substrate. SiC: describing itself as one of the world's largest merchant makers of SiC epitaxial wafers for power semiconductors, it is preparing mass production of 8-inch (200mm) in addition to 6-inch (150mm) SiC epi wafers and strengthening production at several domestic sites, including a new Yamagata building scheduled to start operation in 2026; the company states its second-generation high-grade epi sharply reduces defect density.
quarterly_data.figure: 3.1 terabytes per platter; 8-inch (200mm) SiC epi mass production readiness; new Yamagata building scheduled to start operation in 2026

quarterly_data.quarter: Resonac (Showa Denko) annual securities report: FY2025 (03-25-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Portfolio reform contracts in FY2025: shares of Fiamm Energy Technology S.p.A. (European automotive and industrial lead-acid batteries) transferred to a special-purpose company under AURELIUS on December 1, 2025; F2 Chemicals Ltd. transferred to Rcapital Partners on September 4, 2025; equipment of the Zhengzhou automotive parts subsidiary transferred to a subsidiary of Guangdong Hongtu Technology on June 30, 2025 (land-use rights and buildings later); and on September 24, 2025 Resonac agreed to transfer its automotive molded-parts business in Japan and Thailand to Moriroku via company splits effective April 1, 2026 (planned).
quarterly_data.figure: Fiamm transfer completed December 1, 2025; F2 Chemicals completed September 4, 2025; automotive molded-parts transfer planned April 1, 2026

quarterly_data.quarter: Resonac (Showa Denko) annual securities report: FY2025 (03-25-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Other segment R&D highlights: Innovation Materials achieved mass production of finer titanium oxide particles for smaller, higher-capacity multilayer ceramic capacitors (MLCC) and started domestic deliveries of the water-based binder resin for lithium-ion battery anodes (POLYSOL LB series) for HEV use; Mobility is supplying samples of a high-performance disc brake pad for EVs to a European Tier 1 brake-system maker; the company began an evaluation experiment on the International Space Station of a semiconductor encapsulant that reduces cosmic-ray-induced soft errors.
